findings.title: OS command injection (output-based)
findings.description: Parameter 'ip' is passed to an OS shell. The shell echoed the injected canary argosCMDb4f9597ac8 back in the response — the command executed on the server. This is full remote code execution as the web-server user.
findings.remediation: Never build shell commands from user input. Use language-native APIs (subprocess with a list argv, no shell=True), strict allowlists for any required arguments, and least-privilege service accounts.
findings.evidence_response:
HTTP 200 
argosCMDb4f9597ac8

findings.title: SQL injection — error-based SQL injection (SQLite error disclosed)
findings.description: Parameter 'q' is vulnerable to error-based SQL injection (SQLite error disclosed). The application echoes a database error when the parameter is broken out of its query — the input is embedded in SQL unsafely.
findings.remediation: Use parameterized queries / prepared statements for every database access; never concatenate user input into SQL. Apply least-privilege DB accounts and input validation as defense in depth.

findings.title: SSTI → remote code execution
findings.description: Parameter 'name' is evaluated by a server-side template engine (probe "{{7*'argosSSTI'}}" executed). The sandbox escaped and an OS command ran — the echoed canary argosRCEc0440f9fe0 appears in the response. Full RCE as the web user.
findings.remediation: Never render user input as a template. Use sandboxed environments (SandboxedEnvironment), disable dangerous globals/filters, and apply least privilege.

findings.title: Path traversal / arbitrary file read (Windows)
findings.description: Parameter 'file' accepts directory-traversal sequences — payload '..\\..\\..\\..\\..\\..\\windows\\win.ini' returned contents of a protected OS file (marker found: '[fonts]'). Attackers read source code, /etc/passwd, credentials, or any file the service account can access.
findings.remediation: Reject '..' sequences and absolute paths; canonicalize the resolved path and verify it stays inside the intended base directory; prefer allowlisting file identifiers over paths.

findings.title: SSRF → local file read (file://)
findings.description: Parameter 'url' fetches attacker-controlled URLs. Payload 'file:///c:/windows/win.ini' produced internal content ('[fonts]'). The server read a local file through the URL parameter.
findings.remediation: Allowlist outbound destinations (scheme+host+port), block link-local/metadata ranges (169.254.0.0/16, 127.0.0.0/8, 10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16), disable redirects, and never return raw fetch results to the client.

findings.title: XXE → local file read (Windows)
findings.description: The XML parser at http://127.0.0.1:5000/api/xml resolves external entities — the injected entity returned a protected OS file ('[fonts]'). Attackers read source code, keys and credentials, and XXE can escalate to SSRF/RCE.
findings.remediation: Disable DTDs and external entity resolution in the XML parser (libxml2: XML_PARSE_NONET/noent off; DocumentBuilderFactory: disallow-doctype-decl=true).
